figures.claim: One ZIM produces one SQLite metadata index and one FAISS vector index; the service loads them for search.
Separates true redirects, meta-refresh pages, HTML articles, and skipped MIME types.
Identifies FTS5 column indexing, temporary vector blobs, redirect targets, and stable document IDs.
A single first-paragraph representation, prefix, tokens, ONNX hidden states, and normalization.
Distinguishes resumable SQLite batch commits from final FAISS persistence.
Shows the actual 10,000 embedded-article threshold and cluster policy.
Separates cosine, FTS5 BM25, and ZIM full-text ranking before fusion.
Explains the global mutex over search execution and avoids claiming parallel speedups.
Defines a proposed measurement framework, not measured hardware performance.
Shows how to isolate variables when profiling Zimantic.

runtime_coverage: educational fixture only, no ZIM or ONNX inference
